description: Adopt biome lint + 4 ratchet gates (file-size, debt-marker, coverage, dead-code) + dup gate (jscpd), wired into the CAM-59 check:all spine.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity (complexity group, stable, maxAllowedComplexity default 15) and noExcessiveLinesPerFunction (complexity, stable since v2.0.0, options maxLines default 50, skipBlankLines, skipIifes). CLI flag --error-on-warnings promotes warnings to errors. Grandfather via overrides[].includes globs. Both rules require explicit enable (not in recommended).
Reports unused dependencies, exports, and files. Runs via bunx knip, configured via knip.json. Supports Bun + TypeScript (TS as peer dep). knip v6 requires Node 20.19+ or Bun.

Copy-paste detector based on Rabin-Karp. Run via bunx jscpd@5. Configured via .jscpd.json with threshold:<pct> and reporters:["threshold"]; the threshold reporter exits non-zero when duplication exceeds the threshold percent.

userStories.title: Adopt biome as a lint-only gate (lean ruleset + grandfather overrides)
userStories.description: As a fleet maintainer, I need biome wired in as a lint gate (lint-only, NOT formatter) with the two named complexity rules enabled as errors and a snapshot of current violators grandfathered via overrides, so the project gains a static linter today without forcing a repo-wide reformat or hundreds of recommended-rule findings.
acceptanceCriteria: biome.json exists at repo root with `linter.enabled: true`, `formatter.enabled: false`, `linter.rules.recommended: false`, and the two complexity rules enabled with severity 'error': complexity.noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity and complexity.noExcessiveLinesPerFunction (the latter with an explicit `maxLines` option). [oracle: file-assert] (jq -e '.linter.rules.complexity.noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity == "error" and .linter.rules.complexity.noExcessiveLinesPerFunction.level == "error" and (.linter.rules.complexity.noExcessiveLinesPerFunction.options.maxLines | type) == "number" and .linter.rules.recommended == false and .formatter.enabled == false' biome.json)

The `maxLines` option for noExcessiveLinesPerFunction is pinned to a concrete documented value `<= 100` (target: 80), proving the rule is not trivially disabled by setting an absurdly large limit. [oracle: file-assert] (jq -e '.linter.rules.complexity.noExcessiveLinesPerFunction.options.maxLines <= 100' biome.json)

The grandfather `overrides` are a per-file allowlist of CONCRETE paths, not a catch-all wildcard. No `overrides[].includes` entry equals `**`, `**/*`, `**/*.ts`, `**/*.tsx`, or `src/**` (anything that would silence the whole repo). [oracle: file-assert] (jq -e '[.overrides[]?.includes // [] | .[]] | all((. == "**" or . == "**/*" or . == "**/*.ts" or . == "**/*.tsx" or . == "src/**" or . == "src/**/*") | not)' biome.json)
@biomejs/biome is installed as a devDependency. [oracle: file-assert] (jq -e '.devDependencies["@biomejs/biome"] != null' package.json)

A `lint` script is added to package.json that invokes biome with --error-on-warnings (e.g. `bunx biome lint --error-on-warnings`). [oracle: file-assert] (grep -F -- '--error-on-warnings' package.json && jq -e '.scripts.lint != null' package.json)
`bun run lint` exits 0 on the current tree (grandfather overrides snapshot current violators). [oracle: bun run lint]

A new GATES entry named `lint` exists in scripts/check-all.ts (added via the existing `g()` helper) so the gate auto-propagates to CI through the spine. [oracle: file-assert] (grep -E "g\('lint'," scripts/check-all.ts)
ci-parity stays green: the new `lint` script is a gate name and therefore allowed in CI. [oracle: bun run check:ci-parity]
`bun run check:all` exits 0 with the new lint gate included. [oracle: bun run check:all]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: biome.json (new, repo root), package.json (add devDependency + `lint` script), scripts/check-all.ts:79 (GATES manifest, use g('lint', 'bunx biome lint --error-on-warnings')). Operator constraints (MUST honor): (a) biome is LINT-ONLY (formatter NOT a gate, never run); (b) lean ruleset: recommended: false; enable ONLY the two named complexity rules. Do NOT enable biome's recommended ruleset (would surface hundreds of findings to grandfather; explicit future follow-up). `maxLines` target: 80 (must be <= 100 per AC). Picking a sane N rather than the biome default 50 reflects current cam-cli style (functions in src/supervisor/loop.ts run long but bounded) while still proving the rule is on. Grandfather pattern: `overrides[].includes` must be a per-file allowlist of CONCRETE paths from the violator scan (enumerate each oversized file by exact path, e.g. `src/supervisor/loop.ts`, `src/commands/dashboard.ts`); the gate AC explicitly forbids catch-all globs (`**`, `**/*`, `**/*.ts`, `**/*.tsx`, `src/**`). Per biome 2.x docs the grandfather targets the rule, not the file globally. Use `noExcessiveLinesPerFunction` with `{ level: 'error', options: { maxLines: 80 } }`. Re-check docs/agent-readiness.md `## Score` table (Style & Validation row) and scripts/cam/patterns.md `Gate-spine convention` bullet. Gate-spine invariant: adding to GATES auto-propagates to CI via the spine; do NOT add a separate `bun run lint` step to ci.yml.

userStories.title: File-size ratchet (raising a ceiling requires tracker ref in diff)
userStories.description: As a fleet maintainer, I need a file-size ratchet that snapshots current per-file LOC ceilings into a committed budget, fails when any tracked file exceeds its ceiling, and ALSO fails when the staged diff of the budget RAISES a ceiling without citing a tracker reference (CAM-NNN, #N, or http(s) URL), so file growth is either prevented or deliberately approved with a paper trail.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/check-file-sizes.ts exists and is the gate entrypoint. [oracle: file-assert] (test -f scripts/check-file-sizes.ts)

scripts/file-size-budget.json exists and snapshots the current per-file LOC ceilings as a `{ path: ceiling }` object (or equivalent documented shape). [oracle: file-assert] (test -f scripts/file-size-budget.json && jq -e 'type == "object"' scripts/file-size-budget.json)
When every tracked file is at or below its budget ceiling, the gate exits 0. [oracle: bun scripts/check-file-sizes.ts]

When any tracked file exceeds its ceiling, the gate exits nonzero and names the file:line in stderr (verified by a unit test that injects an in-memory budget vs. an in-memory size map). [oracle: bun test]

When the staged diff of scripts/file-size-budget.json RAISES any ceiling and contains NO tracker ref (`CAM-\d+`, `#\d+`, or `https?://`), the gate exits nonzero (verified by unit test that injects a fake `getStagedDiff(path) => string` returning a raised-ceiling diff with no tracker ref). [oracle: bun test]

When the staged diff of scripts/file-size-budget.json RAISES any ceiling and contains a tracker ref, the gate exits 0 (verified by unit test that injects a raised-ceiling diff containing a tracker ref). [oracle: bun test]

When the staged diff of scripts/file-size-budget.json contains only same-or-LOWERED ceilings, the gate exits 0 regardless of tracker ref (lowering is always allowed; verified by unit test). [oracle: bun test]
A new GATES entry named `file-size` exists in scripts/check-all.ts. [oracle: file-assert] (grep -E "g\('file-size'," scripts/check-all.ts)
`bun run check:all` exits 0 on the current tree with the new gate included. [oracle: bun run check:all]
ci-parity passes. [oracle: bun run check:ci-parity]
Typecheck passes. [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: scripts/check-file-sizes.ts (new), scripts/file-size-budget.json (new, snapshot current tree), test/check-file-sizes.test.ts (new, mirror source), scripts/check-all.ts (add GATES entry). DI pattern (MUST mirror scripts/check-all.ts SpawnFn DI, also used by US-004 coverage gate): export pure functions and inject (a) a sizes source `getSizes: () => Record<string, number>`, (b) a budget reader `readBudget: () => Record<string, number>`, and (c) a git-diff source `getStagedDiff: (path: string) => string`. The CLI entrypoint wires real adapters (`Bun.file`/`Bun.Glob` for sizes, `Bun.spawn` git diff for staged); tests inject in-memory fakes. NEVER shell out to git in unit tests. Ratchet logic: parse the staged diff of scripts/file-size-budget.json; if any per-file `-` / `+` pair indicates a raised ceiling (new value > old value), require at least one `CAM-\d+|#\d+|https?://` token elsewhere in the staged diff. Same direction as US-004 (coverage lowering): a directional change requires a citation. Symmetric to US-007 docs AC (which already states 'raising a file-size ceiling requires a tracker ref'). Initial snapshot MUST land green: enumerate src/ and scripts/ files (and possibly test/), record current line counts as ceilings, commit. Use `Bun.file` / `Bun.Glob` over node:fs where natural. Honor noUncheckedIndexedAccess (regex/array access is `T | undefined`). Re-check scripts/cam/patterns.md `Oracle-friendly manifest design` and `Gate-spine convention` bullets.

userStories.title: Debt-marker gate: every TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX must cite a tracker id
userStories.description: As a fleet maintainer, I need a gate that scans src/ and scripts/ for TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX markers and fails any marker that does not cite a tracker id (CAM-NNN, #N, or http(s) URL), so debt notes are always traceable to an issue and cannot rot anonymously.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/check-debt-markers.ts exists and is the gate entrypoint. [oracle: file-assert] (test -f scripts/check-debt-markers.ts)

The scanner exports a pure `scanForMarkers` function that the unit tests drive directly (proves the gate's behavior lives in a testable export, not just in a CLI side-effect). [oracle: file-assert] (grep -E 'export function scanForMarkers' scripts/check-debt-markers.ts)
When every marker is cited (or no markers exist) the gate exits 0. [oracle: bun scripts/check-debt-markers.ts]

When a marker is uncited the gate exits nonzero and the stderr line names file:line (verified by a unit test that feeds in synthetic text content via an injectable reader, no filesystem touch). [oracle: bun test]

A marker counts as cited when the same line (or its trailing comment) matches `CAM-\d+`, `#\d+`, or `https?://` (verified by a unit test that feeds cited vs. uncited markers and asserts the classification). [oracle: bun test]

The scanner EXCLUDES `vendor/`, `node_modules/`, `claude-code-harness/`, and `dist/` from its scan; pinning this is critical because src/vendor/_generated.ts contains literal TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX tokens in the embedded auditor prompt that would otherwise fail the gate. Verified by a unit test that feeds synthetic file paths under each excluded directory and asserts they are filtered out before scanning. [oracle: bun test]
A new GATES entry named `debt-markers` exists in scripts/check-all.ts. [oracle: file-assert] (grep -E "g\('debt-markers'," scripts/check-all.ts)

`bun run check:all` exits 0 on the current tree with the new gate (annotate or fix any currently-uncited marker as part of this story; if a marker cannot be honestly cited it is grandfathered with a tracker ref in this story's notes). [oracle: bun run check:all]
ci-parity passes. [oracle: bun run check:ci-parity]
Typecheck passes. [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: scripts/check-debt-markers.ts (new), test/check-debt-markers.test.ts (new). Pattern: pure `scanForMarkers(files: { path, text }[]): { path, line, marker, cited }[]` (exact export name asserted by AC2) + a separate `filterScannablePaths(paths: string[]): string[]` (or equivalent) that drops excluded dirs, both driven by tests + a thin CLI guarded by `import.meta.main` (mirrors scripts/check-all.ts SpawnFn DI). EXCLUSION SET (AC6, MUST pin): `vendor/`, `node_modules/`, `claude-code-harness/`, `dist/`. RATIONALE: pre-existing pattern grep found exactly the expected matches in src/vendor/_generated.ts:24 (7+ literal TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX tokens inside the embedded auditor prompt) plus references to placeholder strings (`US-XXX`, `CAM-XXX`) inside test/oracle prose; the scan must not trip on either. Recognize markers via `\b(TODO|FIXME|HACK|XXX)\b` followed by `:` or whitespace (ignore identifier-internal matches like `US-XXX`). Use `Bun.Glob` to enumerate; honor noUncheckedIndexedAccess (regex capture groups are `T | undefined`, guard with `?? ''`). Pre-scan the current tree (the project context indicates no real markers in src/ or scripts/ outside vendor; verify with `grep -rEn '\b(TODO|FIXME|HACK|XXX)\b' src/ scripts/ --exclude-dir=vendor` before claiming green). Re-check scripts/cam/patterns.md `Oracle-friendly manifest design` and `Gate-spine convention` bullets.

userStories.title: Coverage ratchet (up-only, lowering requires tracker ref in diff)
userStories.description: As a fleet maintainer, I need a coverage ratchet that compares `bun test --coverage` output against a committed floor budget and fails if coverage drops below any floor; raising a floor is always allowed, but lowering a floor requires a tracker reference (CAM-NNN/#N/URL) present in the git diff of the budget file, so coverage erosion is never silent.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/check-coverage.ts exists and is the gate entrypoint. [oracle: file-assert] (test -f scripts/check-coverage.ts)

scripts/coverage-budget.json exists and contains the current measured coverage floors as a documented JSON shape (at minimum a top-level `floors` object or equivalent). [oracle: file-assert] (test -f scripts/coverage-budget.json && jq -e 'type == "object"' scripts/coverage-budget.json)

The runner runs `bun test --coverage`, parses the coverage output, compares each measured metric against its floor, and exits 0 when all measured values are at or above their floors. [oracle: bun scripts/check-coverage.ts]
When any measured value is below its floor, the gate exits nonzero and stderr names the failing metric (verified by a unit test that injects an in-memory coverage source). [oracle: bun test]
Raising a floor is always allowed (gate still exits 0 when measured >= new floor; verified by unit test). [oracle: bun test]

Lowering a floor without a tracker ref in the staged diff of coverage-budget.json fails the gate (verified by unit test that injects a fake git-diff source returning a diff with NO tracker ref). [oracle: bun test]

Lowering a floor WITH a tracker ref (`CAM-\d+`, `#\d+`, or `https?://`) in the staged diff passes the gate (verified by unit test that injects a fake git-diff source containing a tracker ref). [oracle: bun test]
A new GATES entry named `coverage` exists in scripts/check-all.ts. [oracle: file-assert] (grep -E "g\('coverage'," scripts/check-all.ts)
`bun run check:all` exits 0 on the current tree with the new gate (floors snapshot current measured coverage). [oracle: bun run check:all]
ci-parity passes. [oracle: bun run check:ci-parity]
Typecheck passes. [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: HIGHEST-RISK story of this PRD. Files: scripts/check-coverage.ts (new), scripts/coverage-budget.json (new, snapshot CURRENT measured coverage, NOT a target), test/check-coverage.test.ts (new). DI pattern (MUST mirror scripts/check-all.ts SpawnFn DI; same shape used by US-002 file-size gate): export pure functions and inject (a) a coverage source `getCoverage: () => CoverageReport` and (b) a git-diff source `getStagedDiff: (path: string) => string`; the CLI entrypoint wires real adapters, the tests inject in-memory fakes. NEVER shell out to bun test or git in unit tests (would re-enter bun test or require real git). Floor-lowering logic: parse the staged diff of scripts/coverage-budget.json (using e.g. `git diff --cached -- scripts/coverage-budget.json` in the production adapter), if any per-metric `-` line indicates a decrease, require at least one `CAM-\d+|#\d+|https?://` token elsewhere in the staged diff (covers diff-comment-style citations). The snapshot lands GREEN at current measured coverage; do NOT pad floors upward beyond measurement. Re-check scripts/cam/patterns.md `Injectable onResults callback` and `Oracle-friendly manifest design` bullets, and CLAUDE.md `Bun runtime` invariant (`Bun.spawn`/`Bun.$` for the production adapter is acceptable; tests inject fakes).

userStories.title: Duplicate-code gate (jscpd <=4%) wired into check:all
userStories.description: As a fleet maintainer, I need a duplicate-code gate using jscpd that fails when copy-paste duplication exceeds 4% of src/ + scripts/ tokens, so duplication is reviewed instead of silently growing; if current duplication exceeds 4% the threshold is raised to the measured value with a tracker ref note rather than refactored in this story.
acceptanceCriteria: .jscpd.json exists at repo root with `threshold: 4` (or the current measured value if higher, documented inline), `reporters: ["threshold"]`, and patterns scoped to src/ and scripts/ with vendor/, claude-code-harness/, test/ ignored as appropriate. [oracle: file-assert] (test -f .jscpd.json && jq -e '.threshold != null and (.reporters | index("threshold")) != null' .jscpd.json)

Running `bunx jscpd@5` (or equivalent) on the current tree exits 0 (the threshold reporter fails the process only when duplication EXCEEDS the configured threshold; current tree must be at or below). [oracle: bunx jscpd@5]
A new GATES entry named `dup` exists in scripts/check-all.ts that invokes jscpd (e.g. `bunx jscpd@5`). [oracle: file-assert] (grep -E "g\('dup'," scripts/check-all.ts)
`bun run check:all` exits 0 on the current tree with the new gate included. [oracle: bun run check:all]

userStories.notes: Files: .jscpd.json (new, root), scripts/check-all.ts (add GATES entry). Pattern: per jscpd 5.x docs, `.jscpd.json` with `threshold: <pct>` and `reporters: ["threshold"]` makes the process exit non-zero when duplication exceeds the threshold. Scope: `src/`, `scripts/` (use `pattern` glob); `ignore` should exclude vendor/, claude-code-harness/, dist/, test/, .claude/, templates/. If current measured duplication > 4%, raise `threshold` to the measured value (rounded up by 1pp), add an inline comment in .jscpd.json with a tracker ref pointing at a follow-up cleanup issue (file the follow-up as a CAM-NNN under issues.local.json if appropriate); operator-approved fallback per scope brief. Re-check scripts/cam/patterns.md `Gate-spine convention` bullet.
